svg.title: The Group Freeze Point: Stop Together, Finish Together
svg.desc: Each member of a group capture is dumped by its own node's agent after its own preparation. Every member waits at a freeze point; the leader's agent, the driver, releases them all at once when every member has arrived, or aborts them all. After the dump, each member's CRIU waits in its post-dump hook with its process tree stopped and its network locked, until the driver releases them all again.
svg.text: The Group Freeze Point: Stop Together, Finish Together
Twice per capture: before the dump and after it. A member that ends first, or misses a release, aborts the capture for every member.
polls every member's agent until all have reached the freeze point, then posts go to all;
a member that ends first, or a go that is not acknowledged after retries, makes it post abort to all

Each member's agent finishes its member's preparation and holds it at the freeze point. The driver polls each agent until every member has reached it, for up to 30 minutes.
The driver posts go to every member at once; each must acknowledge it.
Each member's CRIU dumps it and waits in its post-dump hook; the driver polls again until every member is dumped.
The driver posts go again, and every member's dump finishes at once. A group capture stops the instance for good (no --leave-running); its replacement pods restore from the capture. An in-
Why both points: members dumped seconds apart saw the gap as real (an etcd expired a client's lease), and a member that went on while another was still being dumped left a TCP connection at
different points in the two images, which never resynchronised after the restore.
